sources.title: Italia Langobardorum: Lombard Italy, 568 to 774
sources.note: Indexed full official site text. Use arrival, Pavia and duchies only. Its imprecise southern ending and sweeping conversion claims are not used.

sources.title: Italian National Tourism Board: Lombard places of power
sources.note: Official chronology, arrival 568 to 569 and Charlemagne taking Pavia in 774. Do not adopt wording suggesting all Lombard culture ended.

sources.title: Italia Langobardorum: Benevento, duchy of Langobardia Minor
sources.note: Direct indexed official heritage account: southern survival after Frankish conquest. Exact foundation year not needed.

sources.title: Italia Langobardorum: Lombard law
sources.note: Use 643 edict, Latin with Lombard words and compensation scaled by social status. Exclude false only-one-copy statement and categorical claims about complete legal equality.

sources.title: Stefano Gasparri, Ca’ Foscari University: Agilulf’s crown and plaque
sources.note: Direct academic source dossier, item 5: extant Bargello plaque inscription VICTURIA DOMNO AGILULF REGI. Crown is lost and separately labelled; do not conflate. Early seventh-century/reign context 590 to 616 in heading.

sources.title: A. Peroni: Agilulf’s plaque, Enciclopedia dell’Arte Medievale
sources.note: Direct full scholarly article, 1991, first four paragraphs: Bargello object, armed attendants, winged Victories, Victuria inscription and Latin language.

sources.title: National Archaeological Museum of Cividale: Lombard bone objects
sources.note: Museum teaching sheet 6: combs and hairpins; six-sided dice and counters; food remains as funeral offerings. Indexed full original PDF. No specific game confidently identified.

sources.title: National Archaeological Museum of Cividale: Gallo cemetery
sources.note: Indexed full museum catalogue: immigrant generation, tomb 9 weaving sword as rank marker, female brooches; tomb A bone counters.

sources.title: Tian and colleagues: Communities and elites at Collegno
sources.note: PNAS 2024 primary research. Direct PMC opens captcha; indexed original query Collegno emerging elites diet returned Abstract and Carbon/Nitrogen Isotope Analysis. Author repository PDF also indexed. Sixth to eighth century community, diverse interrelated families, likely millet, animal protein, no significant sex diet difference.

sources.title: Italia Langobardorum: Monastery of Torba
sources.note: Indexed full institutional history. Eighth-century nuns, reused defensive tower; upper oratory used eighth to eleventh centuries, do not assign all surviving paint to one precise year.

sources.title: Italia Langobardorum: Church of Santa Sofia in Benevento
sources.note: Indexed full official description: Arechis foundation around 760, adjacent convent headed by sister Gariperga, surviving narrative frescoes.

sources.title: Italia Langobardorum: Paul the Deacon
sources.note: Museum-network educational account voiced as Paul; only use documented role as Adelperga’s tutor, following her to Benevento and historical writing. Do not quote invented first-person dialogue as primary testimony.

sources.title: Municipality of Benevento: History of the city
sources.note: Municipal historical account, Lombard and papal periods: 849 division, 1077 end of dynasty. Keep separate from 774 northern conquest.

sources.title: Municipality of Salerno: Castello di Arechi
sources.note: Municipal monument account: Gisulf II surrendered in 1077 to Robert Guiscard.

sources.title: Italian Ministry of Culture: Abbey of San Vincenzo al Volturno
sources.note: Description paragraphs 3 to 5: imperial protection 787, autonomous border abbey after 849, October 881 attack and survivors in Capua. Do not imply direct Lombard governance over the abbey.

sources.title: Museums of Molise: San Vincenzo al Volturno visitor guide
sources.note: Indexed full official bilingual guide. Itinerary 5 Epiphanius crypt, 10 refectory, 12 lavatorium, 13 ninth-century kitchens. Lavatorium is hand and face washing, not a latrine.

sources.title: Marazzi and colleagues: Kitchen and refectory at San Vincenzo al Volturno
sources.note: Primary excavation volume. Printed p27/PDF25 refectory dimensions and circulation; pp43 to 44/PDF41 to 42 Carannante fish bones, drain US2471 and deposit US2522. Do not adopt hypothetical diner count as measured attendance.

sources.title: Schibille and Freestone: Glass production at San Vincenzo
sources.note: 2013 primary study, abstract: 136 ninth-century glasses, Roman tesserae and window glass remelted. Proposed single source building remains interpretation.

sources.title: Marazzi and colleagues: Craft production beside the Volturno
sources.note: 2018 archaeological publication repository abstract: excavation of eighth/ninth-century bell-casting furnace beside river.

sources.title: Salerno Museo Città Creativa: The city and its ceramics
sources.note: Paragraph beginning In particolare poiché il castello: late ninth to early eleventh-century military garrisons, everyday local serially produced kitchen and storage ceramics.

sources.title: Bibliotheca Augustana: Placiti cassinesi
sources.note: University edition after Bruno Migliorini, Storia della lingua italiana, 1960. Item I, Capua March 960: Sao ko kelle terre and modern Italian translation. Modern typographic transcription, not facsimile.

sources.title: Friends of Saint Benedict: The Cassinese judgment of March 960
sources.note: Abbey-associated account with original document image: Rodelgrimo/Aligerno, judge Arechi and three witnesses. Latin act with vernacular testimony, Beneventan hand, archive at Montecassino.

sources.title: Italian Episcopal Conference: Cathedral of Capua
sources.note: Diocesan inventory historical chronology: Landulf foundation 856 and dedication 861; later rebuildings. Do not identify present building wholesale as ninth-century fabric.

sources.title: Abbey of San Vincenzo al Volturno: History
sources.note: Abbey institutional history: Chronicon Vulturnense written around 1130, retrospective source for early abbey; not a contemporary ninth-century manuscript.

proposedOverrides.summary: Southern Lombard principalities supported cities, monasteries and skilled workshops while repeatedly dividing and negotiating power.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Imported early-medieval collective label; decoded 600 footprint and two 700 polygons include northern Italy and southern Benevento zone. Not modern Lombardy and not solely later southern principalities. Kind region chosen for a composite political geography. Public caveat says outline incomplete and named examples extend beyond it, notably Cividale. Northern kingdom 774 conquest distinguished from southern continuation. No runtime Lombard kingdom card found.

Imported 800 and 900 southern-Italy collective polygons, not a northern Lombard kingdom and not one sovereign duchy. Kind region reflects composite political geography. San Vincenzo imperial autonomy is explicit in overview and body; regional archaeology does not assert Lombard jurisdiction. Later eleventh-century endings are clearly beyond the map interval. No alias to lombard-principalities or duchy-of-benevento.
